verdict.rationale: Homebrew's Bottles docs state that when a formula defines a bottle matching your system, `brew install` downloads and installs it automatically. Compiling from source happens only when the user asks for it with `--build-from-source`, and casks likewise install upstream pre-built binaries. That covers installing prebuilt binaries in place of source builds. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of bottle download and install behaviour (the evidence is first-party docs only).

support.subject: As a developer, I can install prebuilt binary packages from a cache instead of compiling from source

citations.quote: When the formula being installed defines a bottle matching your system, it will be downloaded and installed automatically when you run `brew install <formula>`.
Casks are package definitions that install upstream pre-built binaries such as applications, fonts and plugins.
